destination.name: South West Rocks
destination.tagline: A small Macleay Valley coastal town beside Trial Bay, with a gaol ruin and two national parks.
destination.description: South West Rocks is a coastal town near the mouth of the Macleay River, about 40 km from Kempsey, and a popular bathing resort since the 1880s. Trial Bay Gaol, a ruined 1886 gaol built to house breakwater labourers, stands in Arakoon National Park on the bay. Smoky Cape Lighthouse, 111 m above the sea, is the highest lighthouse light in New South Wales, and Hat Head National Park to the south has beaches, dunes and rainforest.
whyVisit: Explore the ruined Trial Bay Gaol
Walk the dunes of Hat Head

goodToKnow.title: Parks and the gaol charge
goodToKnow.detail: Trial Bay Gaol is about 11 AUD (open 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM) and Smoky Cape Lighthouse and Hat Head about 8 AUD each; prices are from the brief and should be rechecked.

goodToKnow.title: Whales pass in winter
goodToKnow.detail: Arakoon National Park lists whale watching in July and August.

goodToKnow.title: Beach camping is possible
goodToKnow.detail: Arakoon and Hat Head national parks both offer beach camping; weather or fire can close Smoky Cape.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} cover whale watching in July and August and the milder months for the gaol and lighthouse walks, while summer brings the beach crowds.

name_evidence: Wikipedia 'South West Rocks' (town on the Mid North Coast); NSW parks pages use the name. No Wikivoyage page exists (it is a red link), so this passes on Wikipedia and NPWS only, a weaker case; the name is the town's real, locally used name.
